learning: No new controller evidence exists for this exact body. The next race is the final unseen-track race, so there is no later tuning loop to learn from.
notes: Final-iteration package: the iteration 5 reference geometry and its controller, unchanged. Chosen because it is the best-evidenced design (score 422.9, oval finish 95%), and every tested variant scored lower.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the Builder's fixed reference geometry (iteration 5) is kept exactly: five sensors at y=0.07 m, x = -0.036 to 0.036 m in 0.018 m steps, 16 mm footprints, track 0.10 m, wheel radius 0.040 m, mass 0.5 kg, body 0.16 x 0.12 m. The controller is the iteration 5 controller unchanged (kp 3.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). Across the design history this combination is the only one that delivered a high oval finish (95%), a strong s-bend progress (0.72) and the best score (422.9). Each controller or geometry variant tested since then lowered the score: mass 0.4 kg (422.1, s-bend progress 0.59), track 0.09 m (347), radius 0.045 m (390), outer spread 0.045 m (309), and seven sensors at 12 mm pitch (331, the most recent race). Iteration 10's seven-sensor telemetry does not transfer to the five-sensor reference, and no controller gain change has been measured on this body. Because the final unseen-track race is scored once and cannot be repeated, I make no untested gain change. Any change to kp, kd or line_loss would be a guess, and a higher kp risks the s-bend overshoot the evidence already shows (max_error pinned near 0.06 m with oscillation near 0.29). Expected result on the development tracks is close to the iteration 5 outcome (about 420 to 425), with oval finish near 95%. This is a prediction only, not a measured result.
